scores.notes: Only a single track runs beside the platform into the distance, leaving the steaming train on the right sitting completely off the rails on the grass/embankment with no track ahead of it. Pale white paper shows at the upper-right corner (accepted).
Two spears appear beside Goliath: one rests on the ground while a second floats diagonally in mid-air behind his left forearm with nothing holding or supporting it.

Daniel (the first-person narrator recounting his vision) stands prominently in the foreground wearing a blue cloak and leather shoulder bag inside the heavenly throne hall, inserting the narrator inside his own spoken vision.
At full zoom, the small folded parchment held by the man in green behind the gold chest is completely blank with no writing, lines, or squiggles.
Mossy green coiled lumps and a green moss-covered sleeping cat replace the croquet hedgehogs on the lawn, alongside men in card capes bending over metal wire hoops.

The Queen's card soldiers behind the Knave and at bottom-right are drawn as human youths with human heads, hats, and sleeved arms wearing card sandwich boards rather than flat oblong cards with hands and feet at the corners, and Alice is child-sized rather than grown large.
Isaiah kneels prominently in the left foreground holding a staff in an Isaiah 6:6-7 coal-bringing scene even though Isaiah 6:2 only describes the six-winged seraphim standing above the throne.

The Queen's card soldiers in the bottom-right corner and behind the tart table have full human heads, hair, hats, and sleeved arms wearing playing-card tabards instead of flat oblong cards with hands and feet at the corners.
Watercolor sky and grass wash reach all four edges cleanly without an unpainted white band or vignette.
Moses's left arm disappears behind the wooden staff with no visible left hand, merging awkwardly into Aaron's lower hand while Aaron grips the staff with both hands.
Unpainted white paper shows behind the foliage in the upper-left corner (accepted by style).
Bill the Lizard in a dark tailcoat is duplicated in the same scene—both stuck head-down inside the jury-box on the right and standing upright on the floor clutching the lower rim directly beneath it.
Pure white unpainted paper shows in the upper-left corner above the tomb rock (accepted by style).

Holmes kneels on the bed facing left toward Watson and his match, lashing his cane into empty air while the bell-pull and snake are directly behind his back on the right wall; the bell-pull also emerges from a ventilator while a second ventilator sits on the adjoining wall.
Playing-card guards at lower-left and center-left bear clear black spade and red heart suit pips on their cards (small unreadable marks).
The three background playing-card guards on the left and center bear red heart suit pips on their white playing-card chests (small unreadable marks).
Collages Isaiah 6:2 with symmetrically duplicated coal-tongs from Isaiah 6:6-7 held by two flanking two-winged angels aiming coals into empty air.
Unpainted white paper shows along the top-left and top-center sky edge (accepted by style).
Pale watercolor sky wash extends to the frame edges and corners.
White unpainted paper shows in the upper-right sky behind the leaves (accepted by style).
Unpainted white paper shows along the top-left sky edge above the distant walls (accepted by style).
Small dark unreadable glyph-like strokes appear on the white paper card tucked into the Hatter's hatband.
A disembodied pink paw protrudes upward from the tablecloth beside the Dormouse's plate while a slice of bread merges directly into the side of the right-hand teapot.
Pure white unpainted paper shows in the upper-left corner above the stone wall (accepted by style).
White unpainted paper shows in the upper-left sky corner above the hills (accepted by style).
Top-center-left sky fades to unpainted white paper along the top edge (accepted by style).

The three background playing-card soldiers on the left bear red heart and dark spot pips (small unreadable marks), and the flamingo's two pink legs form a closed triangle over Alice's skirt and fuse into a single lower leg and foot.

Watercolor extends cleanly to all four edges, but all five men stride rapidly down the road away from the burning house behind their backs without looking at it, contradicting the text's account of hastening toward the blazing house in front of them.
In addition to the human old-man face, the Caterpillar has tangled extra upper limbs—two arms folded across its waistcoat plus a third forearm sprouting upward to hold the hookah mouthpiece.
